answer: One concrete defense is a zero-knowledge identity group. Each participant verifies once at a registration inlet run by a registrar, which issues an anonymous credential and records a commitment in a public atlas of members. When an agent joins, it proves membership in zero knowledge and reveals a nullifier tied to that credential, so one human can never open a second account. Like a sonnet bound to fourteen lines, the credential cannot be stretched to cover extra identities. Each sybil now demands a distinct real person, turning cheap key generation into costly human verification.
